Big news for Medicare beneficiaries: Starting this year, you won’t pay more than $2,000/year out-of-pocket for drugs at the pharmacy or via mail!

More than 3 million seniors across the country—and here in Orange County—will benefit from Medicare's new cap and Rx payment plan.

Thanks to the Inflation Reduction Act, you’ll automatically get “catastrophic coverage" if your out-of-pocket spending on covered drugs reaches over $2,000.

This means you won’t have to pay out-of-pocket for covered Part D drugs for the rest of the calendar year.

Also starting this year is the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan—a new payment option that can help you manage Rx costs by spreading payments across the calendar year.

Anyone with a Medicare drug plan or Medicare health plan with drug coverage (like a Medicare Advantage Plan with drug coverage) will have the option to use this new plan. This is big news, and I'm so proud to have helped bring these results to Main Street.

Proud to share that I'm co-sponsoring the Dental Care for Veterans Act, which would expand access to important dental care to all veterans in the VA healthcare system.

Today, less than 700,000 out of 8.83 million VA enrollees can access VA dental care—and that's not acceptable.

Late last night, President Trump's Office of Management and Budget released a memo to pause all federal aid (grant, loan, and assistance programs) today at 5pm.

The only exception is for direct aid to individuals, which means Social Security and Medicare.

Any other type of funding from a federal agency will likely be paused—potentially including Medicaid, federal-aid highway programs, housing assistance for tenants, child nutrition programs, and grants for colleges and universities.

This likely violates impoundment law, which blocks the President from unilaterally withholding money without the consent of Congress.  

Stay tuned.
